edges.description: Abnormal Ih disrupts the current's normal control of excitability.
Loss of excitability constraint promotes network hyperexcitability.
Early-life seizures and channel dysfunction impair neurodevelopment.
Cortical network hyperexcitability generates spontaneous and provoked seizures.
Sustained early-onset epileptiform network activity drives epileptic encephalopathy.
Altered cortical and thalamocortical rhythmicity manifests clinically with progression toward atypical absence seizures.
Hyperexcitable cortical circuits show heightened seizure susceptibility during febrile illness.
Disrupted early brain development produces global developmental delay.
Impaired maturation of cortical networks leads to intellectual disability.
Altered neurodevelopment produces autistic behavioral traits.
Layer V somatosensory cortical and CA1 hippocampal pyramidal neurons show constitutive HCN1 cation leak, depolarized resting membrane potential, and increased action potential firing from rest.
Displays active epileptiform spiking on electrocorticography, spontaneous seizures, and human-concordant pharmacosensitivity.

nodes.description: The variant alters the Ih current - shifting the voltage dependence of activation, changing gating kinetics, or creating a constitutive cation leak near the resting potential - so that the channel conducts abnormally when it should be regulating excitability. Disease variants have divergent biophysical effects on the current.

nodes.description: Seizures are managed with antiseizure medications; response is variable and the epilepsy is often drug-resistant at the severe end of the spectrum. Importantly, drug selection is genotype-mechanism-sensitive: because the severe form is a gain-of-function cation leak, sodium-channel-blocking antiseizure medications (phenytoin, lamotrigine, oxcarbazepine, lacosamide) can paradoxically worsen seizures and should be avoided, whereas sodium valproate has been reported to help clinically and levetiracetam, diazepam, and ethosuximide reduce epileptiform spiking in preclinical knock-in models.

nodes.description: Org 34167 is a brain-penetrant, broad-spectrum HCN-channel modulator being explored as a mechanism-targeted (precision) therapy: it aims to plug the leaky channel by restoring voltage dependence and reducing the cation leak. nodes.description: Heterozygous knock-in mouse carrying the murine homolog of the recurrent human de novo HCN1 p.Met305Leu DEE variant.
